event.content:
When Caleb regained consciousness, he wasn’t sure where he was (or even what decade he was in). There was an undulant blue blur to his world, like when he used to swim laps in his infinity pool on his Texan ranch. That had cost him a few bitcoins, but nothing like the fortune he’d paid to Cyrogen Futures. His nostrils tingled with an antiseptic chemical odor, like those from the many medical labs he funded. When he was finally able to focus, he saw a white-cloaked woman on a podium, sword at her side, with intricately braided hair. He was behind her, so he couldn’t see her face, but he certainly admired the outline of her taut back.
